html:
SMTO-SKL-0025 — Google Calendar denied access

GUID: 15da0a58-e737-5298-adf2-cacbe8c06958
Slug: google-calendar-provider-forbidden
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Google refused this calendar request for this account, and the reason isn't missing permission from SMTO's sign-in. Reconnecting alone may not help. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO which Google account it used. If it's the wrong one, ask again and name the right account. A different account often can't see or change the calendar you meant.
  2. Open Google Calendar in your browser and check that this calendar is shared with that account with enough permission for what you asked. Google blocks requests the account isn't allowed to make, even if SMTO is connected.
  3. If you use a work or school Google account, ask its administrator whether outside apps may use Google Calendar. An organization's rules can block calendar access for apps even when sharing looks correct.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the calendar task with the account you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your Google administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep reconnecting the account; that alone won't change this permission.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Calendar returned 403 without a scope or read-only reason, so the denial comes from calendar sharing, account or Workspace policy rather than a missing OAuth grant.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 403 without the more specific scope or read-only classifications. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 403 without the more specific scope or read-only classifications.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect account, sharing rules and administrator policy using the safe provider reason.

How to fix it

  • Check which account_ref was used, the target calendar's sharing (accessRole) for that account, and any Google Workspace admin policy restricting Calendar API or external sharing. Additional OAuth scopes alone may not grant access.
  • Check the selected account, Google Calendar sharing permissions and Workspace administrator policy. Additional OAuth scopes alone may not grant access.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check the selected account, Google Calendar sharing permissions and Workspace administrator policy. Additional OAuth scopes alone may not grant access.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual permission boundary is resolved without assuming another OAuth grant will help.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
